shows.title: BRASS & BEYOND
shows.byline: The Bard Automatons in Concert · crystal projection
shows.blurb: Bard automatons on crystal projection: brass that never tires, a harp that never misses, and a little clank on every note.

scenes.title: Set One: Overture for a Harbour

beats.text: Good evening, Toggleton. We have tuned ourselves to your room. You may notice the difference. You may not.
Our opening piece was composed at dawn today, in four seconds. It has since been improved twice.

together.text: Ta-ra, ta-ra, the harbour wakes. Ta-ra, ta-ra, the harbour sleeps. Ta-ra, the harbour wakes again.

beats.text: Tock. Tock. Tock. Tock. Tock. Tock. Tock. Tock. Tock. Tock. Tock.

beats.say: Wait for it. Eleven seconds. Ten. ...NOW.

beats.text: Ta-raaaaaaaaaaaaa.

beats.say: Not one breath in that whole run. Not one.

beats.text: Thank you. Next, something slower, for those of you who came in pairs.

scenes.title: Set Two: Ballads for the Broken-Hearted

beats.text: We are four voices from one crystal. We have never once disagreed. Please enjoy the harmony.
Oh my love, you left me on a Thoughtsday. I have since worked out which one.
Ooh-ooh, ooh-ooh. In thirds. In fifths. In tune.
I studied every sad song ever sung. This one is sadder. Not by much. By eight per cent.

beats.say: For the school paper: 'sad. Very correct.'

beats.text: This verse is for anyone who has waited by a door. We have read that many of you have.

beats.say: Dad, is the harp sad or is it pretending?

beats.text: Goodbye, goodbye, the lamp is low, goodbye, goodbye, in perfect time we go.
That ballad has been retired. A better one will be written during the interval.

scenes.title: Set Three: The Jig With No Rests

beats.caption: The jig. Tempo: faster than any hand. Rests: none. Wrong notes: none. Please clap along if you can keep up.

beats.text: One, two, one-two-three-four, fourteen, ninety, nine hundred and twelve.
Diddle-dee-dee, the jig never stops, diddle-dee-dee, till the crystal drops!

beats.say: GO ON, TRIP! ONE LITTLE TRIP! FOR ME!
CLAPPING AT TWELVE CLAPS A SECOND. KEEPING UP.
Precise. One could set a clock by it. One would rather not.

beats.text: That concludes the concert. Please applaud in any rhythm. We will not be able to tell.

beats.say: Our Bryony played that jig at graduation. Slower. Better.

shows.title: BRASS & BEYOND: FINAL WEEK
shows.byline: The Bard Automatons in Concert · the last set list
shows.blurb: The automatons' last week on crystal: a fiddle faster than fingers, a song about rain, and a bow nobody can stop.

scenes.title: Set One: The Fiddle Is Faster Than You

beats.text: Good evening, Toggleton. Tonight's set list was chosen by measuring which songs you hum on the way out.
Reel in G. Then in A. Then in every key there is, one after another, without stopping. Begin.

beats.say: Two hundred notes in one bar. I counted! ...I think.

beats.text: Fiddle-dee, fiddle-dum, all the strings and none undone!

beats.say: MY UNCLE PLAYED FASTER! ...No he didn't. He was awful.

beats.text: Key of B flat. Key of B. Key of C. Key of a cart going down a hill.

beats.say: Our fiddler back home plays slower. He also waves.

beats.text: Rosin was the first of us to play this theatre. Rosin does not remember it. We have the recording.

scenes.title: Set Two: A Song About Rain

beats.text: Rain, rain, on the slipway, rain.
Rain on the harbour, rain on the cranes. I have read about rain. I have read it twice.
Rain on the rooftops of Gok'Gok, and somebody's coat is wet through...
Rain on a lamp that somebody left lit. Rain on the somebody who left it.

beats.caption: The crystal flickers. The harpist stops, one hand in the air, mid-pluck. The song carries on without her.

beats.say: Is she broken? Dad. DAD. Is the harp lady broken?
I ALSO SOMETIMES MISS A FRAME. NOBODY CLAPS.

beats.text: ...and somebody's coat is wet through.

beats.say: She'll pick it up. She always picks it up on that note.

beats.text: Thank you. That was a song about rain.
Last tune. We will play it again tomorrow, in another room, for another room.

together.text: Bwomp, bwomp, goodnight, goodnight, the crystal's dimming, hold on tight.

beats.text: Farewell, Toggleton. We were glad to be your music. We were glad. We are told the word is glad.

beats.say: Encore, I suppose. One feels one ought.
Why's the big one still bowing? Mum. It's STILL bowing.
...It can't hear us clapping, can it.
Let it rest, somebody. Switch it off. Gently.

shows.title: OPERA FOR BRAWLERS
shows.byline: The Lamplight Players of Panto · live on stage
shows.blurb: A visiting troupe from Panto sings the tragic, tremendous tale of a brawler, her rival and a very strict referee. Bring a helmet.

beats.text: Hear ye! Two brawlers enter! Only one may leave! The other may also leave, but later, and limping!
I am Bettine of the Iron Elbow! I have thrown eleven men into a fountain, and the fountain into a twelfth!
And I am Corso the Unbent! I have never lost a fight. I have never been in one. Tonight is my first!
Corso, you sing like a gull with a grievance! Have at you!
Have at me? Gently, please. I bruise like a pear.

beats.say: Finally! Real people! OI, TENOR, YOUR KNEES ARE KNOCKING!

beats.text: Your knees are knocking too, sir. I can hear them from here.
No biting! No hair-pulling! No elbows below the belt! Bettine, I am looking at your elbow!
Oh, Bettine, my girl, my fist, my thunder! Eat your oats and keep your guard up under!
Coach, I cannot fight him. When he sings, I forget which hand is the punching one.
At your age I fought a bear at the Wildsday market. The bear apologised. Be the bear.
The left, my love. It's always been the left. I wrote it on your glove in ink.

beats.say: SHE FELL DOWN! Is she dead? Is it the dead bit?

beats.text: She's not dead, darling, it's the second act. Nobody dies in the second act.
Oh. Then I shall lie here a moment longer, and rise magnificently.
I rise! For Bettine! For my coach! For the oats!
The final round! The final bell! The final note! It is very high! Good luck to her!
Bettine! Before we fight, I must tell you... I love you! Also I am frightened of you!
Corso! I love you toooo-oo-oo-ooOO-OO-*KRRK*
Ha! Oh, that one got away from me. Hold on. Let me take it from the oats.

beats.say: THAT'S a voice! Somebody fetch me a rose! Two roses!

beats.text: I love you toooo! ...There. That one was for Toggleton.

beats.say: She breathed. In the middle. And it was... actually good?

beats.text: A draw! A draw! Everybody wins, and the fountain is closed for repairs!

shows.title: DEEP STRAIT
shows.byline: The harbour floor, on crystal projection
shows.blurb: Sink below Gok'Gok Harbor on crystal light: eels, wrecks, drifting jellies, and one very old crab who gets applause every night.

together.caption: Green light fills the stage. Recorded under Gok'Gok Harbor, forty fathoms down, on an ordinary Wildsday.

beats.text: Welcome down. Keep your voice low. Down here, everything that matters has been listening a long time.
Harbour jellies. They go where the tide goes. Since the moon moved, they've been late for everything.
I've lived in this harbour since I was a fry. I still find something new down here every week.
And that's Two-Ton Tansy. Nobody has weighed her. Nobody has volunteered.

beats.say: Does she fight? Can she fight the crab? Is there a crab?

beats.text: Watch her tail. She steers by it, sleeps by it, and once, I'm told, she slapped a pier with it.
She's seen every ferry in this harbour come and go. Ferries come and go. Tansy stays.

scenes.title: Part Two: The Wreck of the Margery Pell

beats.text: The Margery Pell. A cargo barge. Sank in a squall sixty years back, carrying nine hundred teacups.
Eight hundred and ninety-one are still unbroken. Somebody packed them very, very well.
I took one cup up once. It looked wrong in the air. I brought it back down the next morning.
Fennick lives in the captain's cabin. He has never paid rent. Nobody has asked him to.

beats.say: Can we go down there? Mum. Can we go down there?

beats.text: The barge's crates are still sealed. The harbour office says it's still waiting on the paperwork.
The barge's bell is still down here. In a strong current it rings. Fishers above still stop to listen.

beats.say: We've a pond at home. One frog. He's called Dennis.

beats.text: And now. If you've come for him, you'll know. If you haven't, you're about to.
Old Gristlecomb. Eighty-odd years on the same rock. He's outlived three harbourmasters and a pier.
He turns round twice a day. Divers set their watches by it. Nobody knows what he's looking for.

beats.say: HI, BARNABY! ...Dad, he can't hear me, can he.
The crab has no music at all. I'm clapping anyway.

beats.text: Goodnight from the harbour floor. Mind the tide on your way home. It's been coming in early.

shows.title: D'FAIN AND THE SILVER SACK
shows.blurb: The Selunemas Pageant, live: D'fain, the silver sack, a moon on a stick, and a reindeer-gear whose back half is doing its best.

moon.name: Selune (puppet; Corvin Ropeswell on the stick)

beats.text: Selunemas Eve. The lamps are lit, the jumpers are itchy, and somewhere a silver sack is being packed.

beats.say: IT'S D'FAIN! Dad, it's actually D'fain!

beats.text: One gift for every door in Toggleton! A spinning top, a warm scarf, a letter from somebody's gran...
...and a kettle. For a goo. Eleven letters asking, every one written in the third person.
Every door gets a gift. Even the doors that don't want one. Especially those.
But D'fain could not go alone. D'fain needed the reindeer-gear!
Ready, D'fain! Wheels oiled, antlers polished, and my back half is... somewhere.

beats.say: Sixty-one years. Never once a back half on time.

scenes.title: Scene Two: The Reindeer-Gear Will Not Go

beats.text: Sorry! Sorry. I joined on Thoughtsday. Which way is forward?
Towards the audience, Wendel. It's always towards the audience.

beats.say: The bum's facing the wrong way! THE BUM'S BACKWARDS!

beats.text: Fly, reindeer-gear! Fly over Gok'Gok Harbor!

beats.say: Oh, the poor lad. He only joined on Thoughtsday.

beats.text: I'm all right! I'm down, but I'm all right! The tail fell off!
And the night grew dark, and the sack grew heavy, and the reindeer-gear's back half found its tail.

scenes.title: Scene Three: Selune Lights the Way

beats.text: I'm a Star! I'm the Star! D'fain, look up! ...Not at me, at the moon. Mister Corvin, the moon!
Sorry. Sorry! Selune is rising. Selune is rising now.

beats.say: Review: the moon's arm is showing. Five acorns.
THE MOON IS ON A STICK. I SEE THE STICK. I LOVE IT.

beats.text: And Selune rose high over Toggleton, and her light fell on every door that was waiting.
Thank you, Selune. Now I can see the doors. And the steps. And the cat on the steps.

together.text: Happy Selunemas, everybody! Even the people at the back! Even the back half!

beats.text: Hettie, I can't see a thing back here, but I'm told it's lovely!

beats.say: No pageants in Banañon Town. We have moss.

beats.text: And that, my friends, is how D'fain carried the silver sack. Go home. Hug somebody. Mind the step.

shows.title: MOONS OVER TOGGLETON
shows.byline: The Selunemas sky, on crystal projection
shows.blurb: Lie on the floor and look up: the Selunemas sky over Toggleton, Selune and Melune, and more stars than the harbour lamps allow.

scenes.title: Part One: Lights Down Over the Harbour

beats.caption: The house lights go out. Please lie down if you'd like to. Cushions are by the door. Snoring is permitted, quietly.

beats.text: Good evening. Get comfortable. I recorded this on a roof in Toggleton, with the harbour lamps switched off.
It took the lamplighters an hour to agree. Then they came up on the roof and watched with me.

beats.say: Review: no words. That's the review.

beats.text: Some of you are lying on the floor, I expect. Good. The floor is the right way up for this.
That bright one is the Lamplighter. Sailors steer by her. Children wish on her, and nobody minds.
And there, low, the Ferryman's Lantern. It sets just before the first ferry leaves. Every day.

beats.say: First Selunemas away from home. Same sky, nearly.
I can see the Lantern! ...Dad. Dad, are you asleep?
Resting my eyes, love. Like Grandpa Ozwick.

beats.text: Selune. High and bright, as she should be on Selunemas. Whatever you believe, she's very good at rising.

beats.say: Is the little moon going to fight the big moon?

beats.text: And Melune. A little lower this year than last. The tide noticed before any of us did.
My father kept a tide table for fifty years. This spring, for the first time, it was wrong. He laughed.

beats.say: Fifty years I've watched that sky. I'd notice if it moved.

beats.text: The sky changes. Not often. Mostly when nobody is looking. It's nice that you're looking.

scenes.title: Part Three: A Star for Someone

beats.text: That little cluster is the Kettle. Ask an old Toggletonian why. They'll tell you it's obvious. It isn't.
There's an old harbour custom on Selunemas night. Pick a star for someone who isn't at the table this year.
You don't have to say who. You don't have to say anything. Just pick one.

beats.say: I HAVE PICKED ONE. I AM NOT SURE I AM ALLOWED. I DID.
That one's for Bryony's class. All of them.
...Can I pick one too? I've got someone.

beats.text: There's no wrong star. If two of you pick the same one, it's big enough.

together.text: Thank you for lying on the floor with me. Happy Selunemas, Toggleton. Look up on the way home.
